# Results — Study 724 (Pumpkin-Spice-Season): does the PSL launch buy a tradable autumn in SBUX? 1993–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly **total-return** series for
**Starbucks (SBUX)**, the **S&P 500 (SPY)** and the **13-week T-bill** (^IRX, the cash leg), built from
daily auto-adjusted closes resampled to month-end on a verified hole-free grid: 1993-02 → 2026-05,
**400 months**. The object of study is the **excess** SBUX − SPY ("beats the market"). As-of
2026-06-01; inputs fingerprint `1d50b4e1e153`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Pumpkin premium"? `BUSTED`

The pumpkin-spice folklore says the late-August PSL launch kicks off an Aug–Nov season in which
Starbucks beats the market. The tape says **there is no such season**. The Aug–Nov excess over SPY
averages **+1.25%/month** vs the off-season's **+0.69%** — a spread of **+0.56%/month with Welch
t = 0.65** — and its block-bootstrap 95% CI is **[−0.84%, +1.92%]**, straddling zero. No individual
calendar month clears even a nominal |t| ≥ 2 (the largest is *March* at t = 1.71 HAC, off-thesis), and
the PSL-launch month August is the **weakest** of the four season months (t = 0.54). A 12-window
placebo ranks Aug–Nov only **#2** of twelve four-month windows — an off-thesis **Mar–Jun** window
(+0.74%) is stronger. The market-neutral "hold the SBUX-vs-SPY pair only in the season" trade earns
**Sharpe 0.27**, *below* the **0.35** of holding the pair all year — the season *dilutes* the edge
rather than concentrating it. And the season spread is **negative** in 1993–2009 (−0.69%) and only
turns positive in a snooped 2010-on half. `NONE`, `MIRAGE`, pumpkin premium `BUSTED`.

## Data stamp

- **Series**: SBUX + SPY + T-bill (^IRX) monthly total-return, 1993-02 → 2026-05, **400 months**,
  as-of 2026-06-01, fingerprint `1d50b4e1e153`
- **Construction**: daily auto-adjusted closes resampled to month-end (last close of each calendar
  month). Grid asserted hole-free on every read by `fetch_data`. SBUX and SPY are **total-return**
  (dividends & splits reinvested) — labeled accordingly, not price-only. Object of study: excess
  SBUX − SPY.
- **Survivorship (Signal axis)**: SBUX is a single hand-picked survivor — one of the great stocks of
  its era — so the raw-return win is read with maximum suspicion and the market-relative + placebo
  tests carry the verdict.

| Jun | +1.59% | +1.06 | +0.92 | 33 | No |
| Jul | −1.83% | −0.97 | −0.86 | 33 | No |

Not a single month clears |t| ≥ 2, naive or HAC. The largest excess (March, +2.45%, t = 1.71) is not
part of the pumpkin story and would not survive Bonferroni for 12 tests (α = 0.05/12 ≈ 0.004 ⇒
|t| ≈ 3). The launch month August is the *weakest* of the four PSL months.

## Season vs off-season spread (the headline)

| | Mean monthly excess | n |
|---|---|---|
| Season (Aug–Nov) | +1.25% | 132 |
| Off-season (Dec–Jul) | +0.69% | 268 |
| **Spread** | **+0.56%** | — |
| **t-stat (Welch)** | **0.65** | — |
| **Block-bootstrap 95% CI** | **[−0.84%, +1.92%]** | 5000 resamples, 12-month blocks |

The direction is nominally as folklore predicts (season > off) but the magnitude is small and the CI
swamps it. **The spread is indistinguishable from noise.**

|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | Mar-Apr-May-Jun | +0.74% | +0.79 |
| **#2** | **Aug-Sep-Oct-Nov (PSL)** | **+0.56%** | **+0.65** |

| #4 | Jan-Feb-Mar-Apr | +0.49% | +0.51 |

| #8 | Nov-Dec-Jan-Feb | −0.36% | −0.40 |
| #9 | Jul-Aug-Sep-Oct | −0.39% | −0.42 |

A real seasonal edge would put Aug–Nov at the top. It ranks **#2**, behind a spring window that has
nothing to do with pumpkins. When the story-window isn't the winning window, the story is decoration.

## Rotation / timer race (Sharpe = excess of T-bill)

Long-only rotation: long SBUX in Aug–Nov, SPY otherwise (calendar-known, no execution lag). Net charges
5 bp one-way × NAV. The market-neutral pair holds long-SBUX/short-SPY; the "season only" version is on
in Aug–Nov, cash otherwise.

| | CAGR | Sharpe (excess) | max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|
| seasonal rotation (SBUX Aug–Nov, else SPY) | +15.1% | 0.66 | −64% |
| rotation (net 5 bp) | +15.0% | 0.65 | −64% |
| market-neutral pair, **season only** | +5.6% | **0.27** | −35% |
| market-neutral pair, **ALL YEAR** | +6.2% | **0.35** | −68% |
| buy & hold SPY | +10.9% | 0.61 | −51% |
| buy & hold SBUX | +17.6% | 0.58 | −76% |

The rotation's Sharpe (0.66) only nudges past SPY's (0.61) because it substitutes a higher-returning
stock into four months — *borrowed SBUX beta*, not seasonal alpha, and not even the best four months.
The honest isolation of "the season" is the market-neutral pair held **only** in Aug–Nov: Sharpe 0.27,
*lower* than holding the same pair all year (0.35). If the alpha lived in the season, restricting to it
would raise the Sharpe; it lowers it.

## Sub-period — the season spread is unstable and sign-flipping

| Period | Season mean | Off mean | Spread | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1993–2009 | +0.99% | +1.67% | −0.69% | −0.47 |
| 2010–on | +1.53% | −0.31% | +1.84% | +2.06 |

In the first half the "pumpkin premium" is *negative*; in the second half it nominally reverses to a
+2.06 t — but on a split *we chose*, over half the sample, off a full-sample t = 0.65. Per the desk's
inference bar, a snooped, sign-flipping half reads WEAK at most, never REAL.

## Robustness — the QSR basket

Equal-weight coffee/QSR basket (SBUX, MCD, YUM, CMG) excess over SPY, 2006-02 → 2026-05, **244 months**,
fingerprint `624b662c1d9b`: season +0.71%, off +0.28%, spread **+0.43%/month, Welch t = 0.71**.
Broadening from one name to a basket doesn't rescue the effect — still noise. Whatever autumn pop the
story imagines is neither a Starbucks quirk nor a broad QSR law.

## The honest takeaway

Pumpkin-spice season is a genuine cultural and revenue event — and it leaves *no* fingerprint in
Starbucks' market-relative returns. The Aug–Nov excess-over-SPY spread is t = 0.65 with a CI from −0.8%
to +1.9%, no month is significant, the launch month August is the weakest of the four, the placebo
ranks Aug–Nov behind an off-thesis spring window, the market-neutral seasonal trade *underperforms*
holding the pair all year, and the effect sign-flips across sub-periods. What's real is survivorship:
SBUX beat the market because it was one of the great stocks of the era — every quarter of its year
looks good, and we remember the one with the latte attached. `NONE` on the signal, `MIRAGE` as a trade,
pumpkin premium `BUSTED`.
